## feature

### Controlled two-arm merge benchmark on the GO00009 S19 oligo pool

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: the full protocol ran end to end on the pilot, every stage timed and
logged, and the outputs reconcile with both tools' own summaries.

#### description

```
type: [text, table]
```

1. New analysis repo `20261022.bench_pairloom_vs_fastp.GO00009_S19` (pixi env
   fastp 1.4.0, bwa-mem2 2.2.1, samtools 1.24, pysam, polars) with nine
   tracked scripts covering sampling, both arms, join, inspection, synthetic
   generation, evaluation, timing, and the full-run launcher.
2. Pilot: 100,000 pairs by reservoir sampling, seed 20261022, sha256
   recorded. Both arms consume identical preprocessed mates (fastp PE
   defaults, overlap correction off). 599 pairs filtered in preprocessing.
3. Pilot headline, on 99,401 pairs:

| Category | Pairs | Share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Both merged, identical sequence | 94,015 | 94.58% |
| Both merged, different sequence | 3,686 | 3.71% |
| fastp only | 1,523 | 1.53% |
| PairLoom only | 47 | 0.05% |
| Neither | 130 | 0.13% |

#### before

No controlled comparison existed. The earlier proposal compared tool outputs
with no shared preprocessing, no defined join, and no separate reporting
axes, so disagreements could not be attributed to a mechanism.

#### after

The benchmark runs both arms from one seed-reproducible sample with recorded
versions and commands. It reports agreement, panel consistency, and placement
ambiguity as separate axes, keeps ambiguous pairs, and files representative
disagreements with full evidence under an explicit unresolved category.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `results/sample_stats.json`, `results/provenance.txt`,
  `results/summary.json`, `results/per_pair.parquet` in the analysis repo.
- PairLoom done line: total=99401, mergeable=97748; fastp merged 99,224
  (armA fastp.json). Both counts reconcile with the join universe.
- Rendered pilot summary: `/bioproj/analysis/default/20261022.bench_pairloom_vs_fastp.GO00009_S19/report/pilot_summary.html`

:::

### Synthetic known-fragment tier with AA/GG micro-cases

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: every category expectation from the plan was met or exceeded, with the
two deviations (duplicated-contig stragglers) traced to generator design and
confirmed correct refusals.

#### description

```
type: [table, text]
```

130 synthetic pairs, seed 20261022, 70 bp reads, 200 bp contigs plus one
verbatim duplicate:

| Category (n) | fastp merged / seq correct | PairLoom merged / seq / placement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| clean (40) | 40 / 40 | 38 / 38 / 38 |
| err1 (20) | 20 / 20 | 19 / 19 / 19 |
| err2 (10) | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 / 10 |
| adjacent, 0 overlap (20) | 0 | 19 / 19 / 19 |
| gap, 30 bp uncovered (20) | 0 | 0 |
| duplicated locus (20) | 20 / 20 | 0, all `rescue_ambiguous` |

Every PairLoom miss or refusal originated on the duplicated contig, where
placement is ambiguous by construction.

#### before

The AA/GG behavior existed only inside the unit suite as constructed fixtures
with no end-to-end arm comparison and no error, adjacency, or gap categories.

#### after

The benchmark scores sequence correctness and placement correctness
separately against known fragments. The micro-cases show PairLoom rescuing to
`seq1:1 AACC` with `ZR:i:1` without the duplicate and refusing with
`rescue_ambiguous` with it. fastp and bwa-mem2 cannot process 2 bp reads, so
the micro tier is PairLoom-only by architecture.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `results/synthetic_summary.json` and `results/logs/{micro3,micro4}.stderr.txt`
  in the analysis repo.
- micro3 merged record: seq1, pos 1, AACC, ZR 1. micro4:
  merge-reasons={'rescue_ambiguous': 1}.

:::

## caveat

### Panel-consistency mildly favors PairLoom by construction

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: the mechanism is certain, its magnitude is not quantified.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

PairLoom conditions merging on a unique joint placement, so its merged
sequences re-align uniquely by construction. fastp merges without a
reference. Panel-distance comparisons therefore say more about placement
policy than about sequence quality. Per the protocol, no merge was labeled
invalid for differing from a designed oligo, and unique mapping was not
treated as truth.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

SE re-alignment of merged sequences: PairLoom 96,020 unique full matches,
0 multi, 0 unmapped. fastp: 96,035 unique, 602 multi, 89 unmapped
(`results/summary.json`).

:::

### QUAL strings are not comparable between arms

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: measured on every both-merged pair.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

Zero of 94,015 both-merged pairs share an identical QUAL string. The arms
encode consensus confidence differently. Compare qualities within an arm, or
recalibrate before comparing across arms.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`results/summary.json`: identical_qual_strings 0, different_qual_strings
94,015.

:::

## conclusion

### The two tools agree on 94.6% of pairs and disagree through three mechanisms

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: the pilot join is complete, reconciles with both tools' own counts, and
each mechanism was verified on representative examples with full evidence.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Both-different (3,686; 3.71%): 3,422 differ at exactly one position. The
   dominant case is an equal-quality mate conflict: fastp calls a concrete
   base at reduced quality, PairLoom emits `N` at q2 when the quality gap is
   under `--min-quality-difference` (5). Worked example
   `A00202:...:11071:34945`: a 1 bp insertion versus the design, both mates
   `38M1I42M`, inserted bases T(q37) versus A(q37); fastp outputs T(q11),
   PairLoom N(q2).
2. fastp-only (1,523; 1.53%): concentrated on placement-ambiguous or
   structurally inconsistent pairs. 666 have both mates under MAPQ 20, 102
   have an unmapped mate, 737 are refused for structural reasons
   (cross-contig concatemers, indel or insertion conflicts, non-primary
   records). Their sequences still mostly match the panel, so the difference
   is placement honesty, not sequence quality.
3. PairLoom-only (47; 0.05%): fastp's ungapped-overlap diff limits reject
   heavily error-laden pairs (overlaps 135-150 bp); PairLoom merges them via
   quality-gated consensus at reduced MAPQ.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `results/summary.json` categories, by_amb_class, rescue_by_outcome.
- `results/disagreements/*.json`: 15 evidence-complete examples per bucket.
- PairLoom merge reasons: different_contig 453, rescue_ambiguous 370,
  rescue_unsupported_alignment 308, non_primary_records 230.

:::

### Synthetic truth confirms sequence and placement semantics separately

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: known fragments make both axes exact; all expectations landed.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Where both arms merged, sequence correctness is 100% for both.
2. Adjacent (0 bp overlap) pairs merge only in PairLoom, 19/20, sequences and
   placements correct. The miss sits on the duplicated contig.
3. Gapped pairs merge in neither arm; PairLoom reports `fragment_gap` and
   never synthesizes the uncovered middle.
4. Duplicated loci: fastp merges all 20 with correct sequences and no
   placement; PairLoom refuses all 20 as `rescue_ambiguous`.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`results/synthetic_summary.json`; missed-qname contigs verified to be `c05`
(`data/synthetic/truth.tsv`).

:::

```
level: high
```

#### description

The end-to-end arm (fastp defaults on raw reads, production style) produced
the same 99,224 merged pairs with identical sequences as the controlled arm
on preprocessed mates. The separate end-to-end comparison adds no merge-level
signal on this sample.

```
level: high
```

## recommendation

### M: Choose the arm by what the analysis needs, not by merge rate

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: grounded in the pilot mechanisms, but the trade-off is use-case
dependent.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

Merge rates differ by 1.5 percentage points, so rate is not the discriminator.
If per-design molecule counting wants maximum sequence recovery, fastp
suffices. If downstream steps consume placements, PairLoom's refusals on
ambiguous loci are the safer semantics. State which semantics an analysis
assumes before choosing.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

fastp merged 99.82%, PairLoom 98.34%; the fastp-only excess is 95%
panel-ambiguous or imperfect on re-alignment (`results/summary.json`).

:::

## observation

### fastp's overlap threshold behaves as strictly-greater on exact boundaries

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: reproduced with a parameter sweep on the synthetic reads.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

With `--overlap_len_require 30`, fastp merged 0 pairs whose overlap is
exactly 30 bp. The same reads yielded 90 merges at threshold 25. The
synthetic overlap was widened to 35 bp to clear the boundary.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Sweep output: req=30 merged_reads=0; req=25/20/10 merged_reads=90
(benchmark session log, 2026-10-22).

:::

### PairLoom rescued 44 pairs with sequences identical to fastp's

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: rescue successes carry `ZR:i:1` and their outputs match the fastp
merge of the same pair.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

Of 731 rescue-eligible pilot pairs, 44 succeeded and all 44 agree exactly
with fastp's merged sequence for the same pair. 687 were refused.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`results/summary.json`: rescue_success 44 (all both_identical),
rescue_refusal_inferred 687.

:::

## process

### Piped samtools view with an explicit dash input failed the first run

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The runner piped bwa-mem2 SAM into `samtools view -b -o out.bam -`.
2. samtools 1.24 refused to read the header from the literal argument `-`,
   exited, and bwa-mem2 died on SIGPIPE after one second.
3. The better action was to omit the input argument so samtools reads stdin
   by default; all three pipeline sites were fixed and the pilot reran clean.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`results/logs/bwamem2_mem.time.txt`: "Command terminated by signal 13";
stderr showed "[main_samview] fail to read the header from \"-\"".

:::

### Orientation was first keyed on the merged record's FLAG strand bit

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The join revcomp'd fastp reads when the PairLoom merged record had the
   reverse-strand bit set.
2. PairLoom merged records are always reference-oriented, so half the pairs
   compared in the wrong orientation and both_different inflated to 51%.
3. The sanity check caught the 50/50 signature; the fix keys normalization on
   R1's primary alignment strand in the pre-PairLoom BAM, and both_different
   collapsed to 3.71%, 93% of it single-position.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Before: both_identical 46,720 / both_different 50,981. After: 94,015 /
3,686 (`results/summary.json` history in the session log).

:::

### Synthetic overlaps were built exactly on fastp's default boundary

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The generator used 30 bp overlaps against `--overlap_len_require 30`.
2. fastp merged nothing, because its check is strictly-greater on this data.
3. The fix widened clean and error overlaps to 35 bp; the boundary behavior
   itself was recorded as an observation instead of being silently tuned
   away.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

First synthetic run: a_merged 0 everywhere; sweep 30/25/20/10 gave
0/90/90/90 merges.

:::
